historical_growth.growth_rate_source: FY26 actual revenue growth (+4%) and the TTV trend (FY25 $9,591m +5%; FY26 transactions +13% with yield dilution), decelerating to 2.5% terminal. Every historical CAGR is distorted: 5-yr windows start in the FY21 COVID trough (revenue $174m), 3-yr windows end on the restated/impaired FY25-26 base, and EPS/equity CAGRs are dominated by the $370m impairment and $255m refund liabilities. The pre-COVID FY19->FY26 revenue CAGR of 6.0% is the only clean long-run read, and it includes the acquisitions of that period.
historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Equity CAGR (-20.8% 3-yr) diverges from revenue (+0.8%) by far more than 30pp: FY25 impairment of $370.0m and recognition of $255.2m customer-refund liabilities cut equity from $1,190m to $579m. Not a growth signal.
historical_growth.notes: FCF CAGRs are on the owner-FCF series (reported FCF less SBC, interest income and lease cash; FY25 also less the $41.9m refund-liability inflow): FY20 48.3, FY22 28.8, FY23 24.9, FY25 45.8. FY24 owner FCF (79.2 - 3.0 - 2.6 - 12.0 = 61.6) was itself flattered by UK over-billing cash later refunded. SBC is immaterial (<0.5% of revenue) so the SBC-adjusted and reported FCF CAGRs do not diverge.

scenario_narratives.base: The core TMC is intact -- 97% TTV retention held through the crisis, FY26 transactions +13%, underlying EBITDA recovered 36% to $113.6m -- but the franchise is diminished: the pre-scandal margin profile was partly fictitious UK revenue, so mid-cycle is the restated 18-19%, not 25%+. Revenue grows ~4% (below the ~7% industry rate) as some renewals are lost; remediation and audit costs fade by FY28; the $187m refund schedule is met from the $175m facility and FY27-28 cash flow; no dividend until FY28. Value is driven by whether an 8% owner-FCF margin on ~$700m of revenue is durable once the UK is cleaned up.
scenario_narratives.bull: Governance reset lands (new CEO, clean FY27 audit, covenants comfortably met), the three non-UK regions compound on their H1 FY26 trajectory -- Asia at 25.6% margin, North America expanding on Lightning/online penetration and the exit from loyalty redemption, Europe repriced -- and the group reaches a 23% EBITDA margin on 6-7% growth. The unsettled ~$40m of refund liabilities settle at the ~85% ratio the key customers accepted, no class action materialises, and the stock re-rates from ~4x to a mid-teens EV/EBITDA as index eligibility returns.
scenario_narratives.bear: The control failure was group-wide, not a UK aberration: the qualified audit opinion on opening balances persists, a shareholder class action and UK regulatory action follow, and corporate/government clients decline to renew as contracts roll in FY27-29 (revenue -4% and -2% in FY28-29). Margins fall back to the FY25 trough of ~13% under sustained legal/remediation cost and pricing concessions. The refund schedule is still met, but the facility is fully drawn, an equity raise ahead of the 2028 maturity is likely, and the business settles as a ~14%-margin, 2%-growth TMC. The bear terminal value binds on the 12x cap, not the zero floor -- the business survives this path but is worth well under the current price.

valuation_philosophy.summary: A governance-recovery turnaround valued on restated, mid-cycle economics rather than on either the fraud-inflated FY19-FY24 margins or the impairment-year FY25 trough. The owner-FCF DCF is built from components (statutory EBITDA margin after remediation cost, lease cash as opex, D&A ex-ROU, 28% cash tax, 5.5% capex) over 10 years because the margin is still recovering; the customer-refund liabilities are deducted as debt, the associated tax receivable is added, NCI is deducted at book, and a $20m allowance for unprovided claims is charged. Risk is charged once: one 10% AUD WACC, with the downside carried in the bear flows and a 35% bear weight. Terminal value is capped at 12x owner FCF (14x bull) for a cyclical with a damaged franchise.
key_risks_to_valuation: Refund liabilities: the ~$40m not covered by the August 2026 settlements is carried at book; the settled $187.2m is undiscounted and treated as certain. A 30 June 2026 balance sheet refresh may move net debt by tens of millions either way.
Litigation and regulatory action are unprovided; the $20m allowance is a house judgment. A large class action or UK government claim would sit mostly in the bear case.

Margin anchor: the restated FY24/FY26 series (17-19% underlying) is the mid-cycle anchor. If the restatement is incomplete -- the auditor's qualification is on the availability of historical evidence -- the true mid-cycle margin could be lower still.
Client attrition is the swing factor between base and bear: 97% retention was the pre-crisis benchmark, and most renewals since the suspension have not yet fallen due.

Liquidity: net current liabilities of $98.2m at Dec-25, refunds of $154m in FY27 funded from a $175m secured facility with leverage, interest-cover and minimum-cash covenants and review events; facility expiry 1 July 2028 (expected 25 Aug 2029). An equity raise ahead of maturity would dilute the flat share count assumed here.
Data vintage: the FY26 annual report (30 June 2026 balance sheet and cash flow) is not yet extracted; FY0 revenue/EBITDA come from the results announcement via the Analysis JSON.

Plus ~0.06m nil-price performance rights; the remaining ~1.03m PRs carry $11.99-$13.99 hurdle prices (4-5x the current price) and are treated as lapsing. Held FLAT: SBC is expensed in the flows.
inputs.total_debt_note: NOT bank debt (nil drawn at 31 Dec 2025). This is the customer-refund liability arising from the CTM UK over-billing: settled refunds payable $154.2m in FY27 + $33.0m in FY28 = $187.2m (FY25 AR subsequent-events note, AUD basis) plus ~$40.3m of customer-related ($17.1m) and other refund ($23.2m) liabilities not covered by the August 2026 full-and-final settlements, carried at book. It is deducted undiscounted as a debt-like item. The new $175m facility that funds it is not double-counted: drawing the facility converts this liability into bank debt one-for-one.
inputs.cash_note: Cash and cash equivalents $121.191m at 31 Dec 2025 (H1 FY26 note 4) less $8.407m client cash held for suppliers (restricted) less $20.6m the group itself classes as restricted and not freely available (FY25 AR note 10) = $92.2m free cash.
inputs.reported_fcf_note: FY2025 actual (latest full-year cash flow statement; FY26 not yet extracted). Company-definition FCF = OCF 141.567 - capex 38.895 (PPE 1.449 + intangibles 37.446) = 102.672. Two adjustments before the owner-FCF identity: (i) lease cash under treatment B, principal 10.036 + interest 1.723 = 11.759; (ii) the 41.893 operating inflow from 'increase in payables, customer related liabilities and provisions' -- money collected from UK customers that is now being refunded, not cash earned. 102.672 - 11.759 - 41.893 = 49.02. last_fcf = 49.02 - 1.095 SBC - 2.143 interest income = 45.78 (7.2% of FY25 revenue).

Forward path set at 0.5% of revenue to allow for the new CEO/retention grants flagged for the FY26 remuneration report.

The 30 June 2026 balance sheet in the FY26 annual report (released Sep 2026) must be refreshed into cash/refund liabilities/NCI when that filing is extracted; the refund schedule is from the August 2026 subsequent-events notes in both filings.
inputs.wacc_rationale: AUD flows discounted at an AUD-built rate: AU 10y ~4.3% + 5.5% ERP x beta ~1.3 (small-cap TMC, cyclical) = ~11.5% cost of equity; ~20% debt weight post the $175m facility at ~8% pre-tax (5.6% after tax) -> ~10.0% WACC. ONE rate across all three scenarios: the governance, litigation and client-attrition risk is carried in the bear flows and a 35% bear weight, not stacked into the discount rate (owner-fcf.md 7f).
inputs.lease_treatment: B -- leases as operating cost. Full lease cash (FY25 principal $10.036m + interest $1.723m = $11.76m = 1.85% of revenue) charged inside EBITDA via lease_cost_pct_path (1.8%); lease liabilities ($37.2m at 31 Dec 2025) excluded from net debt; da_pct_path is ex right-of-use depreciation (FY25 D&A 64.658 less ROU 10.738 = 53.9m = 8.5% of revenue).
inputs.nci_treatment: Flows are group-level; the $17.45m NCI book value at 31 Dec 2025 is deducted once in the equity bridge (NCI profit share ran $1.8-2.7m/yr, so book is close to a capitalised value). Not also folded into a leakage rate.
inputs.notes: MODEL: owner-FCF DCF, component build (Drivers route), 10-year horizon because margins are still recovering from the FY25 trough. Operating company (travel management) -- routing table row 2, cyclical non-US, with section 7 adaptations. WHY FY25 IS NOT THE BASE: the FY25 year carries a $370.0m impairment (non-cash, backed out), $255.2m of newly recognised UK customer-refund liabilities and ~$13m of restructuring/audit costs; underlying EBITDA fell to $83.6m (13.1% of revenue) versus a restated FY24 $116.4m (18.3%). The impairment WAS a lagging confirmation of weaker fundamentals -- the restated FY24 (NPAT 86.4 -> 20.9m, revenue 710.4 -> 637.1m) shows the pre-scandal 25-29% EBITDA margins were partly fictitious UK revenue -- so the mid-cycle margin is anchored on the RESTATED series (FY24 18.3%, FY26 17.0% underlying, H1 FY26 19.5%), never on the as-originally-reported numbers. BASIS CHOICE: restated. FY0 = FY2026 (revenue $669.9m, underlying EBITDA $113.6m from the Sep-2026 result). EBITDA margin paths are on a STATUTORY-EBITDA basis (post-IFRS-16, before lease cash, AFTER the remediation/forensic/restructuring costs the company excludes from 'underlying'), which is why year-1 sits ~1.5pp below the underlying margin. Customer-refund liabilities are treated as debt (see total_debt_note); the $48.5m income-tax receivable that the refunds generate is added in the bridge; a $20m unprovided allowance for shareholder/regulatory claims is deducted (no class action confirmed as at Sep 2026, but the group is co-operating with regulators in Australia and the UK). Terminal cap 12x (bear/base) and 14x (bull) for a cyclical with a damaged franchise. SBC-light market: house and street bases are ~1% apart.

bear.margin_rationale: Client losses at renewal (UK public sector first), remediation and legal cost persisting, pricing concessions to retain accounts: margin falls back to the FY25 trough (13%) and settles at 14%. Growth turns negative in FY28-29 as multi-year contracts roll.

base.growth_rationale: FY26 +4% actual; industry mid/high-single-digit growth offset by post-scandal client attrition as contracts renew; decelerates to 2.5%.
base.margin_rationale: Statutory-EBITDA basis. FY26 underlying 17.0% less ~1.5pp of continuing remediation/restructuring cost in FY27, then recovery to a 19% mid-cycle -- between restated FY24 (18.3%) and H1 FY26 (19.5%), well below the pre-restatement 25-29% that the UK over-billing inflated.
base.da_capex_rationale: D&A ex-ROU 8.5% in FY25 includes amortisation of acquired client relationships (reduced by the FY25 impairment); glides to the 5.5% capex run-rate (FY25 6.1%, H1 FY26 5.5%) so the terminal year carries no permanent tax shelter.
base.tax_rationale: Blended statutory (AU 30%, UK 25%, US ~24%, Asia ~17%) ~28%; refunds' tax recoveries are in the bridge, not the rate.
base.wc_rationale: Payables ($422m) exceed receivables ($344m): an agency float, so growth releases a little cash. 3% capture, deliberately small because part of that float is the refund money.

bull.margin_rationale: Asia already runs 25.6%, NA 20% and rising on Lightning/online penetration, Europe restored to 30%+ on project work in H1 FY26, ANZ back toward its 25%+ history: a 23% group mid-cycle. Cap 14x for a re-rated, clean-audit CTM.

required_return_table.note: Each row rebuilds the terminal value at that row's rate (max(0, min(Gordon@r, 12x FCF_N))); the WACC row is valuation.base.intrinsic_value and the hurdle row is entry_price.base.entry_price.

sensitivity.note: Rows are WACC, columns terminal growth; each cell rebuilds its own terminal value.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: House default is 15/50/35; moved to 35/45/20. Bear raised to 35% because the situation carries three of the named triggers at once -- a qualified audit opinion and a fraud-driven multi-year restatement (control environment unproven), a covenant-laden facility funding $187m of refunds with the directors' own stress test showing only ~$40m of EBITDA headroom, and unquantified regulator/class-action exposure. Bull cut to 20% because it needs several independent things to go right (clean FY27 audit, no litigation, all three regions expanding margin, and a market re-rating of a name just removed from the ASX 200). Base 45% is the balance.

sanity_check.basis: SBC-adjusted on both sides (EPS less SBC/share; EBITDA less SBC), so these deliberately do not match GAAP screener multiples.
